title: Louis Armstrong's styles and favorite records
summary: Bergen explains that Louis means Armstrong, prefers his best style, praises Eldridge, and names West End Blues and other favorite records.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: What about Louis Armstrong? You say you like Louis, but there's a lot of Louis's really. I mean through the years there's many different kinds of Louis Armstrong.
I'm glad you clarified that because I was thinking about that when I said Louis. When I say Louis, that means Louis Armstrong. If I mean prim, I say prima.
But we always did say play like Louis plays. Every time I've mentioned it on this interview Louis, I met Louis Armstrong.
But I mean there's many different styles. I mean Louis, which style do you like?

Well Louis, to me, he had the best style. Now Eldridge, I thought he was terrific. I didn't hear Eldridge on too many records, but After You're Gone, Eldridge made a terrific record on After You're Gone. I even heard James on one or two records and it sounded pretty jazzy to me. He had a different style when he was with, what you call his band, Goodman's band. I didn't like that style too much, but it made him. But on a record I have with him and Coleman Hawkins I believe, he sounded pretty good.
But back to Armstrong, what tunes do you like that Louis made?
Well naturally I liked West End Blues. But I have a record Mr. Our Mr. Ambassador or something like that.

And Muscat rambles out of this world man. It's terrific. And I think I like that better than that. They have good teamwork too. The band hits it off good with him and he plays a lot of good. Of course he throws in a few little tunes but he dresses them up so nice that they're jazzy. They're not just inserting a couple of measures of another tune. He makes them fit in right. I used to always like Someday You'll Be Sorry. I thought it was very fine. And I have a lot of records that you're probably not up on like Red Rose, Red Nose, Red Cap, on a little beach in Wakalu, Hawaii or something like that. Anyway he plays terrific stuff on these records. You know I like those Hawaiian things.
A little bamboo bridge. To you sweetheart. He plays good stuff.

To you sweetheart. You know that brother-in-law that went to sleep when he was 14 years old on a bandstand? When he got to be about 25 he'd never be playing a band but he'd take his trumpet and he'd play all them Louis, you know the ones that weren't too high? You know those easy ones like on a little bit. And he had them down pretty good. But he'd have to learn something by heart real good because you'd jump meter. It's a funny thing. Some musicians jump meter. Oh boy that's something. You can't really correct that.
